headline: MU set to gap down about 6% after Monday's 19% surge
tldr: MU closed Monday at $707.70 (+19.04%) on the Nvidia relief rally, last printed $664.48 (−6.11%) at 6:54 ET, and I expect an open about 4% to 9% lower (roughly $644–$679), centred near −6.3%, with $650.00 as the first support underneath.

headline: MU set to gap up about 6% after Friday's 14% rout
tldr: MU closed Friday at $594.51 (−13.89%), its lowest close since early May, last printed $630.45 (+6.05%) at 6:50 ET, and I expect an open about 3.5% to 8.5% higher (roughly $615–$645), centred near +6%, with $650.00 as the first test overhead.

headline: MU points 5% lower as Asia's chip rout deepens
tldr: MU closed Thursday at $690.44 (−2.10%) after reversing from a $760.01 high, last printed $653.80 (−5.31%) at 7:17 ET, and I expect an open about 3% to 7.5% lower (roughly $639–$670), centred near −5%, with the Nov 5 low of $650.00 as the level to watch.

headline: Anthropic's $83 pricing lifts MU 4.8% pre-market to $739
tldr: MU closed Wednesday at $705.27 (−1.00%), last printed $738.82 (+4.76%) at 7:21 ET after Anthropic priced above its range, and I expect an open about 2% to 6% higher (roughly $719–$748), with a centre near +4% because the last three opens landed 1.0 to 1.6 points under the early print.

headline: Nvidia beat lifts MU to $730 pre-market; the bounce is fading
tldr: MU closed Tuesday at $712.42 (−0.92%) after a round trip to $666.88, last printed $729.98 (+2.46%) at 7:06 ET on Nvidia's beat, and I expect an open about 0.5% to 4.5% higher, leaning to the lower half because the bounce has shrunk all night.

headline: MU bounces to $733 pre-market after 7.6% drop; Nvidia reports tonight
tldr: MU closed Monday at $719.02 (−7.62%) after a new US AI-chip export rule and a DRAM antitrust ruling, last printed $733.39 (+2.00%) at 6:52 ET, and I expect an open flat to about 4% higher, though that print is stale and Nvidia reports after the close.

headline: Asian chip rout points MU about 4% lower into Nvidia week
tldr: Memory sold off hard across Asia (SK Hynix −7.89%, Kioxia −7.7%, Taiex −6.03%) and MU's last print was $744.00 (−4.41%) at 6:32 ET after Friday's $778.31 close, so expect a gap down of roughly 2.5% to 6.5% the day before Nvidia reports.

headline: Huang is out at Nvidia; MU steadies near $800 before PPI
tldr: Nvidia's CEO resigned Thursday and chips absorbed it (MU closed $798.44, −1.59%, after opening −5.18%), and MU's latest pre-market print is $806.07 (+0.96%) with futures slightly positive ahead of October PPI at 8:30 ET (7:30 SK).

headline: Nvidia CEO turmoil drags chips; MU indicated down about 4%
tldr: Reports that Nvidia's board may remove Jensen Huang have NVDA down about 8% pre-market and Nasdaq 100 futures down about 0.8%, pulling MU to $780.50 (−3.8% from Wednesday's $811.30 close) with no Micron-specific news.

headline: CoreWeave beat lifts chips; MU indicated up about 6%
tldr: CoreWeave's revenue beat and raised 2026 guide have Nasdaq 100 futures up about 1.8% and MU near $771 pre-market (+6.4% from Tuesday's $725.11 close), one day after a hot CPI sent the 10-year yield above 5%.

headline: CPI at 7:30 SK decides whether Monday's chip rebound holds
tldr: Chips had their best day in months on Monday (SOX about +6.9%, MU +6.25% to $733.15) and Asia followed, but Nasdaq 100 futures are −0.3% and MU has faded to about $726 ahead of an 8:30 ET CPI print that a Fed governor has tied to a possible 50bp December hike.

headline: Nvidia down 5% on Huang probe; MU flat ahead of CPI
tldr: Nvidia's board opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy and the stock is down about 5% pre-market, but the rest of the chip complex is shrugging it off (Taiex +4.9%, Nasdaq 100 futures +0.4%), MU is roughly flat at about $685, and Tuesday's CPI (with December hike odds near 80%) is the bigger event.

headline: Chips bounce about 5% pre-market after SOX's worst day since 2020
tldr: SOX fell 12.25% to 9,011 Thursday and MU fell 17.5% to $656.39, and Asia sold off again overnight, but US chips are bouncing pre-market: SMH and SOXX are up about 5%, MU is about $703–$710 (+7–8%), and Nasdaq 100 futures are up about 1.5% even after a hot jobs report (+165K) pushed yields higher.

headline: Chip selloff deepens; MU indicated about 5% lower, near 200-day average
tldr: Asian memory stocks crashed for a second day, Qualcomm's weak guidance and a Bloomberg report that Micron paused its new Taiwan plant add to the pressure, and with Nasdaq 100 futures down about 1% and SMH down 3.7% at about 9:10 ET, MU (about $755) and SOX (about 9,900 implied) are set to open at fresh lows while the Dow keeps rallying.

headline: Blue wave hits AI infrastructure; MU indicated about 2.5% lower
tldr: Democrats won both chambers, and a Texas governor who has promised a data-center moratorium won too. That pulled money out of the AI build-out trade overnight. Nasdaq futures faded to about flat by 8:45 ET while the Dow rallied, and MU slid from +1.4% early to about −2.6% ($832.78) by 8:30 ET, even though AMD, Arista and Super Micro all beat.

headline: MU up about 3% pre-market after Monday's 5.8% drop; AMD reports tonight
tldr: Monday's chip bounce failed, MU closed at $833.59 (−5.78%) and Seoul and Taipei each fell 3.6% overnight. MU is still indicated about 2–3% higher near $850–$860 on a flat-to-firm Nasdaq, but tonight's AMD, Arista and Super Micro results and the election make this open easy to fade, as Monday's was.

headline: MU indicated about 2% higher as chips bounce despite Kioxia
tldr: Futures are up after Friday's chip rout, helped by Korea's strong chip exports, SK Hynix's 3.8% gain and lower oil, so MU is set to open about 2–3% higher near $905, with Kioxia's flat NAND outlook as the main risk.

headline: Kioxia's weak outlook hits memory after Friday's chip sell-off
tldr: US markets are closed today (Sunday) and reopen Monday at 9:30 ET (8:30 SK). Futures are up modestly after Friday's sell-off in chips, SK Hynix has recovered in Seoul, and Kioxia's flat profit outlook is the main new risk for memory stocks.
